verses: In the old capital they stood, With yellow fox furs plain, Their manners all correct and good, Speech free from vulgar stain. Could we go back to Chow's old days, All would look up to them with praise.
In the old capital they wore T'ai hats and black caps small; And ladies, who famed surnames bore, Their own thick hair let fall. Such simple ways are seen no more, And the changed manners I deplore.
Ear stoppers, made of sew stones fine, In the old days were worn. Each lady of a noble line A Yin or Chi seemed born. Such officers and ladies now I see not, and my sorrows grow.

With graceful sweep their girdles fell, Then in the days of old. The ladies' side hair, with a swell, Like scorpion's tail, rose bold. Such, if I saw them in these days, I'd follow with admiring gaze.
So hung their girdles, not for show;— To their own length 'twas due. 'Twas not by art the hair curled so;— By nature so it grew. I seek such manners now in vain, And pine for them with longing pain.
